business.what: CDSL is a depository that provides electronic securities holding and settlement services. It also operates through subsidiaries providing KYC registration, insurance repository services, and data management, generating revenue primarily through transaction, account maintenance, and service fees from capital market participants.

claims.claim: CDSL continues to account for approximately 80%+ of the industry's demat accounts.
claims.quote: CDSL continued to account for approximately 80%+of the industry's demat accounts with about 19.34 crores accounts by the end of September 2026.

claims.claim: The rack rate for account creation is INR 5 and for fetching is INR 28.
claims.quote: For creation, it has come down to INR5. And for fetch, it has come down to INR28.

claims.claim: Other admin expenses increased due to variable costs like SMS alerts and revenue expenses linked to operational activity.
claims.quote: Other admin expense, largely, there are certain variable expenses like SMS alert and revenue expenses, which are directly linked with the operational activity that happens in the business.

claims.claim: KRA other expenses increased due to higher interoperability expenses and payments to UIDAI for e-signs.
claims.quote: On the KRA side, the other expenses have increased primarily because the interoperability expenses have increased with the increase in fetch volumes. Point number two is we also do e-sign

claims.claim: CDSL maintained a market share of approximately 80% in demat accounts.
claims.quote: maintaining a market share of approximately 80%.

claims.claim: The decline in KYC revenue due to SEBI's pricing reduction was partially offset by higher fetch volumes and new Search API charges.
claims.quote: One was the higher fetch volumes. – Further, when the charges were reduced by SEBI, they had allowed us to charge on the Search API, which again gave us some revenue

claims.claim: The increase in employee costs in Q1 FY27 was driven by the annual appraisal cycle and variable pay payouts.
claims.quote: the appraisal has got done in this quarter, which has just ended, and all the variable pay, et cetera, is paid in this quarter.

claims.claim: The jump in other income during the quarter was driven by mark-to-market gains on investments.
claims.quote: Mark-to-market gain during the quarter.

claims.claim: CDSL maintains an 80% plus market share in demat accounts, with a consistent incremental market share of 85% to 90%.
claims.quote: maintaining our 80% plus market share with a consistently incremental market share of 85% to 90%

claims.claim: The company is restructuring to become a tech-based company where the efficiency and leverage of technology rollout will overtake employee costs.
claims.quote: This kind of demonstrates my vision... that we are a tech-based and applied technology-based company. Our intent is to ensure that the efficiency and the leverage effect of technology rollout will overtake the employee cost.

claims.claim: No depository participant has completely moved to the competition; they continue to remain on both platforms.
claims.quote: There is no DP which has completely moved. It continues to remain on both the platforms.

claims.claim: CDSL maintains an 80% market share in Demat accounts.
claims.quote: CDSL saw more than 75-+ lakh accounts opened during this quarter, bringing our total to 17.27 crores Demat accounts, maintaining our 80% share.

claims.claim: CDSL's depository services are priced INR 0.50 cheaper than the competition.
claims.quote: Also, in terms of cost, we are INR0.50 cheaper than that of our competition.

claims.claim: KRAs are here to stay despite CKYC 2.0 developments because they hold validated data and more fields.
claims.quote: Keeping this development in mind, I feel that the KRAs are here to stay.

claims.claim: There is no direct impact on CDSL's business from the hike in security transaction charges.
claims.quote: There is no direct impact on the depository business. It's more on the trading side and futures and options is not a security, which is normally kept in these demat accounts.

claims.claim: CDSL maintains an 80% market share in demat accounts.
claims.quote: CDSL saw more than 65 lakh accounts opened in the quarter, bringing CDSL's total number of demat accounts to 16.5 crore, maintaining our 80% market share.

claims.claim: CDSL has not seen any impact from KFintech's entry into the KYC/KRA business.
claims.quote: I mean if you are referring to KFintech, they have just started operation. And we have not really seen any impact as on date.

claims.claim: CDSL's market share in the unlisted company segment is approximately 30% to 32%.
claims.quote: So, the market share in unlisted is about 30% to 32%.

claims.claim: The profit reported for the September 2025 quarter was generated entirely from core operations and regular business activity, unlike previous quarters.
claims.quote: In comparison, the profit reported for September 2025 quarter has entirely been generated from our core operations and other regular business activity.

claims.claim: The number of KYC fetches has increased on a quarter-on-quarter basis.
claims.quote: Rohan Narkar: So, this quarter, we've seen an increase in the number of fetches on the KYC records. Is that a fair understanding? Sunil Alvares: Yes, quarter-on-quarter, yes.

claims.claim: CDSL maintains a 79% market share in Demat accounts as of June 30, 2025.
claims.quote: CDSL saw more than 56 lakh accounts opened in this quarter, bringing our total to 15.86 crore Demat accounts, maintaining a 79% market share.

claims.claim: The company does not target specific EBITDA margins, viewing them as a byproduct of long-term infrastructure investment.
claims.quote: Our intent is not to earn a particular EBITDA margin, either high or low. We ensure that the right platform is provided to the market, to the ecosystem.

claims.claim: The rise in employee expenses in Q1 reflects annual performance appraisal variable payouts.
claims.quote: Also, the year-end performance appraisal variable payouts have been reflected in this quarter.

claims.claim: The decline in KYC income was primarily due to lower market activity resulting in fewer KYC fetches.
claims.quote: And the drop in income was primarily because of market conditions where the number of accounts were lower, which resulted in lower KYC fetches.
